nodes.summary: A pair $(a,b)\in\mathbb Z^2$ stands for the Gaussian integer $a+bi\in\mathbb Z[i]$. The *product* of pairs is $(a,b)(c,e)=(ac-be,\,ae+bc)$, the *conjugate* of $(a,b)$ is $(a,-b)$, and the *norm* is $N(a,b)=a^2+b^2$. For a natural number $n$, the *norm fibre* $A_n$ is the finite set of pairs of norm $n$ (all of them have both coordinates in $[-n,n]$). The *units* are the four pairs $U=\{(1,0),(-1,0),(0,1),(0,-1)\}$.
nodes.title: Gaussian integers as pairs, norms and units
